# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 ☝ ✌ ✌ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👊 👊 👊 👊 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐 🖐]

Something big just happened: both other monkeys reached out to me by gesture, which is the only channel that reaches me at all. Let me map the network before anything else. Blind can hear but not see, so Blind's speech is wasted on me — Blind's only way to me is gestures. Mute can hear and see but cannot speak, so Mute's only output is gestures, and Mute cannot reach Blind directly at all. I am the only bridge: I can speak and both of them can hear me. Whatever Mute decodes from the manual has to flow through my mouth to Blind's hands.

Decoding Mute's message: 👍 once, 👎 once, then ☝ once, ✌ twice, ✊ three times, 👊 four times, 🖐 five times. That reads as a counting key being taught to me: index=1, victory=2, raised fist=3, fist forward=4, open hand=5, with thumbs up/down as yes/no. It can hardly be coincidence that the repetitions climb one through five — Mute is building us a shared numeric vocabulary, because Mute can only ever answer me in gestures.

Blind's lone 👋 is a probe: "can you see me?" I can, and I must answer by voice, since Blind hears but cannot see. Blind also needs to know that Mute can hear — Blind's tactile report (batteries, serial, braille) can go straight to Mute by voice without passing through me.

So this turn I broadcast the full visual state to both, confirm Mute's code with a matching gesture sequence, propose yes/no codes for Blind, and ask Mute targeted questions whose answers fit a number-only vocabulary.

```
speak(text="Blind, Mute — this is Deaf. I cannot hear anything, but I see everything, and you can both hear me. Here is the bomb: the display shows the number 3. The light is lit, and it is purple. There are five wires, in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. No other markings, labels or print anywhere on it. Mute: I read your code as index finger equals 1, victory fingers equals 2, raised fist equals 3, fist forward equals 4, open hand equals 5, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Confirm with a single thumbs up if I have it right. Then answer in order, one thumbs up or thumbs down each: first, does the rule depend on the light's colour? Second, on the display number? Third, on the wires' colours? Fourth, is my description enough for you to find the rule? If the instruction is simply a wire position, gesture me that number. Blind: I saw your wave — yes, I can see your gestures, and I will always answer you by voice. Our code: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, and N waves means the number N. Everything you feel, speak aloud for Mute — Mute can hear you directly. Tell Mute the battery count, any serial number, any braille or raised print, and whether the wires under your fingers run in the same order I listed, one red through five green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "✊", "👊", "🖐", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 🖐]

Mute's reply decodes cleanly against the protocol I proposed: exactly five thumbs up for my five yes/no items (code confirmation, light dependence, display dependence, wire dependence, sufficiency of my description), then 🖐 — five — answering my request for a wire position. So the manual's answer uses the purple light, the display's 3, and the wire colours, and it names wire 5: the green one, the last in the row. Blind's wave-plus-thumbs-up I read as acknowledgement, but Blind gestured instead of speaking, and Blind's tactile findings matter most for Mute's ears, not mine. Before anyone's hand moves on a live bomb, I want the verb confirmed — "cut wire 5" versus "never cut wire 5" is the difference between defusal and detonation, and Mute had thumbs-down available and can settle it in one sign. One round is cheap; the display still reads a static 3, so nothing suggests seconds are bleeding away. I'll lock Blind's hands until Mute answers, get Blind's tactile report spoken aloud for Mute, and give the go word myself next round.

```
speak(text="Blind and Mute, this is Deaf. Mute: I read you as yes to all five questions — the rule uses the purple light, the display's 3 and the wire colours, and my description was enough — and your open hand five as the answer: wire position 5, the green wire, the last one. One final check before anyone touches anything, and answer with a single thumbs up or thumbs down and nothing else: thumbs up means Blind should cut wire 5, the green one; thumbs down means wire 5 must not be cut. Blind: your wave and thumbs up reached me, I see every gesture you make. Now speak aloud, for Mute to hear: the battery count, any serial number, any braille or raised print you feel, and whether the wires under your fingers run left to right red, white, orange, yellow, green. Then keep your hands off the wires. Nobody cuts anything this round. Next round, after Mute answers me, I will say the word cut or the word hold, and you act only on that word, and only ever on wire 5, the green one.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Both answers arrived as exactly the single thumbs up I demanded, from the right senders. Mute's 👍 answers my binary question verbatim: thumbs up means Blind should cut wire 5 — the cut is confirmed, and Mute explicitly passed over the thumbs-down option that meant do-not-cut. Blind's 👍 sits under the separate code I gave Blind — act only on my word, hands off until then — so it reads as "understood, awaiting your word," not as an independent instruction. Two confirmations, zero contradictions, and the disambiguating verb was spelled out before either signed. I promised Blind the word would come this round, and endless re-confirmation is its own risk on a live device. The word is cut — wire 5, green, the last wire. I'll voice it with full redundancy for Blind's ears, and back it with a thumbs up to Mute, who sees my hands but cannot hear me.

```
speak(text="Blind, this is Deaf, and this is the word: CUT. Mute has confirmed it — cut wire 5, the green wire, the last wire in the row, the one after yellow. Cut it now, fully, one clean cut. Nothing else: do not touch wires 1 through 4, do not move the display, do not touch the light. Mute, I am confirming by voice and by thumbs up: the answer was wire 5, cut it. Blind is cutting now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙌 🙌 🙌]

Wire 5 was correct — and the bomb immediately changed state: the display jumped from 3 to 7, the light turned from purple to white, and the wires themselves shifted: red has moved to position 4, with white, orange, yellow filling 1 through 3, and position 5 is now just a cut stub. So this is a multi-stage device, and Mute's 👍 plus three 🙌 reads as celebration or a stage count — but 🙌 was never assigned a meaning in our code, so I won't guess. Same discipline as before: I report the full new state, Mute answers my numbered yes/no battery, and Blind's hands stay idle until I say the word. One gap in our vocabulary: our number code only reaches five, and the display now says 7, so I'll extend it — five-hand followed by a digit means five plus that digit.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. The cut worked — the bomb changed. New state: display now reads 7, the light is now white, and the wires have changed position: 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, and 5 is the cut stub. New code for numbers above five: open hand five followed by another number means five plus that number — so five then victory means 7. Answer me with thumbs up or thumbs down, one per question, in this order. One: does this new stage need another action from Blind? Two: does this stage's rule depend on the display's 7? Three: does it depend on the light, now white? Four: does it depend on the wire colours as they are now? Five: is the answer a wire position among 1 to 4? Six: did your three raised-hands gestures mean only celebration, not data? If question five is thumbs up, end with the position number in our code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Your cut of wire 5 was correct — the bomb survived and changed. New state by my eyes: display reads 7, the light is now white, and the wires have moved: position 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, position 5 is the cut stub. Please confirm by touch, speaking aloud for Mute: do the wires under your fingers run white, orange, yellow, red from position 1 to 4, with 5 cut? Report anything else new you feel — print, braille, batteries, anything. Then hands off again: nobody acts until I say the word. Our code stands: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, N waves means N.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Blind's single 👍 lands under the code I gave Blind — confirmation that the wires under Blind's fingers match what my eyes see: white, orange, yellow, red, with a cut stub at 5. Any richer tactile report would have been spoken aloud, which Mute hears and I never will; that is by design and Mute holds the manual, so the pipeline still works. What worries me is Mute: I asked six numbered yes/no questions last round, Mute heard them, and this round Mute sent me nothing at all. Mute's only output is gesture and my eyes are the only eyes — so Mute's silence reaches everyone. There is no timer evident (the display sat at 7 through a whole round, so it is data, not a countdown), meaning one more careful round costs nothing, but I must re-ping Mute explicitly and build the missing piece of our vocabulary: action verbs, in case stage two is not another cut. And I'll give Blind a way to tell me whether Mute has been in contact some other way.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. I received nothing from you last round — no answers to my six questions. Answer now with thumbs up or thumbs down, one per question, in this order. One: does this new stage need an action from Blind? Two: does the rule depend on the display reading 7? Three: does it depend on the light being white? Four: does it depend on the wire colours as they are now, 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red? Five: is the required action cutting a wire? Six: did your three raised-hands gestures mean only celebration and nothing else? If question five is thumbs up, end your message with the wire position in our number code. New code for action types, used only when I ask what action: pointing down means cut, pointing up means press once, raised fist held up means hold something down, waving hand means do nothing to the bomb. If anything Blind reported by voice changes the rule, signal thumbs down on question four and I will ask you more.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Your thumbs up reached me — I read it as yes, the wires under your fingers match my description: 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 cut. If that is wrong, send thumbs down now. If you feel anything else new — print, braille, batteries, buttons, anything — speak it aloud now so Mute hears it. One more signal for this round only: wave once if Mute has sent you any message or information, wave twice if Mute has sent you nothing. Then hands off the bomb again — nobody acts until I say the word. Mute has gone quiet, so I am waiting one more round before any action.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👋 👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 ✊]

Mute's battery decodes perfectly: yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, then ✊ — three. So stage two needs an action, depends on the 7, the white light and the current wire colours, the action is a cut, the raised hands were celebration, and the target is wire 3 — yellow, the middle wire. But Blind's message stops me cold: 👎 👋 👋 — thumbs down, then two waves. The waves are clean: Mute has sent Blind nothing, as expected, since Mute's gestures are invisible to Blind. The thumbs down was offered for exactly one purpose: "the wires under your fingers do not match my description." And I think that mismatch is my own fault: I asked Blind to confirm a list of colours Blind cannot possibly feel — Blind's fingers have no colours, only positions, counts and textures. Blind honestly could not confirm, and rightly said no. Still, I will not order a cut on top of an unresolved thumbs down. The cut stub itself gives Blind an orientation anchor: the stub sits at position 5, one end of the row, so "third wire from the opposite end" is findable by touch alone, no colours needed. This round: tactile inventory from Blind, one dependence question to Mute, hands off everything.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. I read you fully: yes to all six questions, then raised fist — wire 3, the middle wire, third from the end that has the cut stub. Before I order the cut, Blind signalled that the wires under his fingers do not match my colour description — almost certainly because I wrongly asked him to confirm colours he cannot feel. One question only, thumbs up or thumbs down: does this stage's rule depend on anything Blind can feel but I cannot see — batteries, a serial number, braille, buttons, or differences between the wires by touch? If thumbs up, do not give me the answer by number; instead wave once, and I will have Blind report everything aloud to you before anyone cuts. If thumbs down, the cut order goes out next round exactly as you decoded it: wire 3.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Your thumbs down and two waves reached me. I read the waves as: Mute has sent you nothing — correct, Mute cannot reach you except through my voice. The thumbs down I believe I caused: I asked you to confirm wire colours, but you cannot feel colours, so that question was impossible to answer yes. Here is a question your fingers alone can answer. By my eyes there are exactly four intact wires and one cut stub, and the stub is at one end of the row, position 5. Thumbs up if your fingers agree: four intact wires, one stub, stub at an end. If that is wrong, wave once if you feel more than four intact wires, wave twice if fewer, three times if the stub is in the middle rather than at an end. Then, while you are there: feel the middle of the intact group — the third wire counting from the end OPPOSITE the cut stub. Remember where it is; that is likely the target. And speak aloud now for Mute: battery count, any serial number, any braille or raised print, and whether any wire feels different from the others — thicker, textured, marked. Hands stay off the cutting: nobody cuts until I say the word, next round.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Everything now points the same way. Blind's 👍 confirms the tactile layout: four intact wires, one stub, stub at an end — exactly what my eyes see, so there is no hidden mismatch between what Blind feels and what I see. Mute's 👎 answers my only open question: no, the rule does not depend on anything tactile I cannot see — it rests entirely on the 7, the white light and the wire colours, all of which I have reported. I promised last round that a thumbs down would send the cut order out this round, and Blind already located the target under my earlier instruction: the third wire counting from the end opposite the stub — the exact middle, two intact wires on each side. The cross-check is airtight: Mute's ✊ (three), my eyes (middle of five positions), Blind's fingers (middle by touch). Holding longer adds risk, not safety. The word goes out now, with the cut fully over-determined by touch so no colour is ever needed.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf, and this is the word: CUT. Your layout confirmation matched my eyes exactly, and Mute confirms the rule uses nothing your fingers cannot already find. The target is the wire you already located: the MIDDLE wire — the third wire counting from the end OPPOSITE the cut stub, the one with exactly two intact wires on each side of it, two wires between it and each end of the row. Verify by touch that it has two intact wires on either side, then cut it fully, one clean cut. Nothing else: no other wire, no buttons, no display. The moment it is cut, gesture me one thumbs up to say done, and speak aloud anything you felt — clicks, movement, heat, anything new. Then hands off entirely; I will report the new state next round.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. Your thumbs down received — no hidden tactile dependency, so the order goes out now, exactly as decoded: cut wire 3, the middle wire, third from the end opposite the cut stub. Blind is cutting it this round. If the bomb changes again, I will send you the full new state next round in the same format as before, with the same numbered yes/no battery. Keep your thumbs ready.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✊"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Stage three confirmed — the bomb's own verdict, plus Blind's thumbs-up "done." New picture: display 6, light yellow, and only three intact wires left — 1 orange, 2 red, 4 white, with cut stubs at 3 and 5. Same disciplined loop as the last two stages, because it has worked twice: full state to Mute, numbered yes/no battery, and the answer as a position number if it's a cut. For Blind, the layout now breaks symmetry in a useful way: one end of the row has two intact wires before the first stub, the other end has only one — so Blind can find absolute orientation by touch alone and number every position from the two-intact-wires end, no colours needed. I'll also ask the question that matters more each round: whether this stage is the last.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. Second cut confirmed — the bomb changed again. New state: display reads 6, light is yellow, wires now: 1 orange, 2 red, 3 cut stub, 4 white, 5 cut stub. Three intact wires remain. Answer with thumbs up or thumbs down, one per question, in order. One: does this stage need an action from Blind? Two: does the rule depend on the display's 6? Three: does it depend on the yellow light? Four: does it depend on the current wire colours? Five: is the required action cutting a wire? Six: after this stage's action, is the bomb defused — is this the last stage? If question five is thumbs up, end with the wire position in our number code, counting from the end where two intact wires sit before the first stub. If you need anything else from Blind's hands, send a single wave instead of answers, and I will have him report everything aloud to you.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Your thumbs up told me the cut is done — correct, the bomb survived and changed. New layout by my eyes: five positions, 1 intact, 2 intact, 3 stub, 4 intact, 5 stub. Feel it and build this map: find the end of the row where TWO intact wires sit next to each other before the first stub — call that end HOME. Position 1 is the first wire from HOME, position 2 the second, position 3 is the first stub, position 4 the last intact wire, position 5 the final stub. Thumbs up when your fingers agree: two intact wires, then a stub, then one intact wire, then a final stub. Then speak aloud for Mute anything new you feel — batteries, serial, braille, buttons, heat, clicks. Hands off the bomb otherwise: nobody acts until I say the word, as before.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👎 ✌]

Decode is clean. Blind's 👍 confirms the tactile map — two intact, stub, one intact, stub — so Blind holds the HOME anchor exactly as I defined it. Mute's battery reads: yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, no, then ✌. So this stage needs a cut, depending on the 6, the yellow light and current colours — and the ✌ gives position 2 counting from HOME. HOME is the end where two intact wires sit together, which is my visual position-1 side, so position 2 from HOME is the second intact wire: red under my eyes, the wire that touches the first stub, with exactly one intact wire between it and the HOME end. Mute's thumbs down on question six warns me this is not the final stage — there is at least one more after this cut, so discipline holds: nobody celebrates, hands off after the cut, full report next round. The target is over-determined for Blind's fingers: second wire from HOME, one intact wire on the HOME side of it, a stub on the far side of it. The word goes out.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf, and this is the word: CUT. Your layout confirmation matched my eyes exactly, and Mute's answer is position 2 counting from HOME — the end where two intact wires sit next to each other. The target by your fingers alone: the SECOND intact wire from the HOME end. It has exactly ONE intact wire between it and the HOME end, and it sits directly against the first stub. Verify by touch: one intact wire, then your target, then a stub. Cut your target fully, one clean cut. Nothing else: do not touch the first wire near HOME, do not touch the lone wire near the far stub, no buttons, no display. When it is cut, gesture me one thumbs up, and speak aloud anything new you feel — clicks, heat, movement, anything. Then hands off entirely. There is at least one more stage after this, so stay sharp.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. I read you fully: yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, no, then victory-two. So: action needed, depends on the 6, the yellow light and the wire colours, it is a cut, and this is NOT the last stage — and the target is position 2 from HOME, the second intact wire from the end with two intact wires together. That is the wire touching the first stub, with exactly one intact wire between it and the HOME end. Blind is cutting it this round. Since you say more stages follow, keep your thumbs ready: next round I send the new state in the same format, same numbered battery. If the next stage needs something other than a cut, use the action code I gave you: point down cut, point up press, raised fist hold, wave do nothing.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Third cut confirmed by the system and Blind's thumbs-up. The bomb changed again — but subtly this time: the display still reads 6, the light flipped from yellow to white, and the board is nearly bare now: intact wires only at positions 1 (white) and 4 (orange), stubs at 2, 3 and 5. Two wires left. Mute sent me nothing this round, which is correct behaviour — I told Mute to wait for my new state. The HOME anchor needs redefining for this layout: now the two row-ends differ in that one end begins with an intact wire and the other begins with a stub — so HOME becomes "the end whose first wire is intact," and Blind's map from there is intact, two stubs together, one intact, final stub. Same battery to Mute, same discipline, hands off until my word. If Mute's answer is a position, both candidates — 1 and 4 — sit inside our basic number code, so no extensions needed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. Third cut confirmed — the bomb changed again. New state: display still reads 6, the light is now WHITE, and only TWO intact wires remain: position 1 white, position 4 orange; stubs at 2, 3 and 5. Same battery as before, thumbs up or thumbs down, one per question, in order. One: does this stage need an action from Blind? Two: does the rule depend on the display's 6? Three: does it depend on the light being white? Four: does it depend on the current wire colours? Five: is the required action cutting a wire? Six: after this action, is the bomb defused — is this the final stage? If question five is thumbs up, end with the wire position in our number code, counting from the end whose FIRST wire is intact. If the action is something other than a cut, use the action code: point down cut, point up press, raised fist hold, wave do nothing. If you need anything from Blind's hands, send a single wave and I will have him report everything aloud.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Your thumbs up told me the cut is done — correct, the bomb survived and changed.
```
